{{Short description|Mathematical conjecture}}
The '''Arnold conjecture''', named after mathematician [[Vladimir Arnold]], is a mathematical conjecture in the field of [[symplectic geometry]], a branch of [[differential geometry]].<ref name="Asselle Izydorek Starostka p. ">{{cite arXiv | last1=Asselle | first1=L. | last2=Izydorek | first2=M. | last3=Starostka | first3=M. | title=The Arnold conjecture in <math>\mathbb C\mathbb P^n</math> and the Conley index | year=2022 | eprint=2202.00422 | page=| class=math.DS }}</ref>

==Strong Arnold conjecture==

Let <math>(M, \omega)</math> be a closed (compact without boundary) [[symplectic manifold]]. For any smooth function <math>H: M \to {\mathbb R}</math>, the symplectic form <math>\omega</math> induces a [[Hamiltonian vector field]] <math>X_H</math> on <math>M</math> defined by the formula

:<math>\omega( X_H, \cdot) = dH.</math>

The function <math>H</math> is called a [[Hamiltonian function]].

Suppose there is a smooth 1-parameter family of Hamiltonian functions <math>H_t \in C^\infty(M)</math>, <math>t \in [0,1]</math>. This family induces a 1-parameter family of Hamiltonian vector fields <math>X_{H_t}</math> on <math>M</math>. The family of vector fields integrates to a 1-parameter family of [[diffeomorphisms]] <math>\varphi_t: M \to M</math>. Each individual <math>\varphi_t</math> is a called a '''Hamiltonian diffeomorphism''' of <math>M</math>.

The '''strong Arnold conjecture''' states that the number of fixed points of a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of <math>M</math> is greater than or equal to the number of critical points of a smooth function on <math>M</math>.<ref name=":0">{{cite arXiv|last1=Rizell |first1=Georgios Dimitroglou |title=The number of Hamiltonian fixed points on symplectically aspherical manifolds |date=2017-01-05 |eprint=1609.04776 |last2=Golovko |first2=Roman|class=math.SG }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite book
 | last = Arnold | first = Vladimir I. | editor-first1 = Vladimir I. | editor-last1 = Arnold | author-link = Vladimir Arnold
 | contribution = 1972-33
 | doi = 10.1007/b138219
 | isbn = 3-540-20614-0
 | mr = 2078115
 | page = 15
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag | location = Berlin
 | title = Arnold's Problems
 | title-link = Arnold's Problems | year = 2004}} See also comments, pp. 284–288.</ref>

==Weak Arnold conjecture==

Let <math>(M, \omega)</math> be a closed symplectic manifold. A Hamiltonian diffeomorphism <math>\varphi:M \to M</math> is called '''nondegenerate''' if its graph intersects the diagonal of <math>M\times M</math> transversely. For nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms, one variant of the Arnold conjecture says that the number of fixed points is at least equal to the minimal number of critical points of a [[Morse function]] on <math>M</math>, called the '''Morse number''' of <math>M</math>.

In view of the [[Morse inequality]], the Morse number is greater than or equal to the sum of [[Betti number]]s over a [[Field (mathematics)|field]] <math>{\mathbb F}</math>, namely <math display=inline>\sum_{i=0}^{2n} \dim H_i (M; {\mathbb F})</math>. The '''weak Arnold conjecture''' says that

:<math>\# \{ \text{fixed points of } \varphi \} \geq \sum_{i=0}^{2n} \dim H_i (M; {\mathbb F})</math>

for <math>\varphi : M \to M</math> a nondegenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

==Arnold–Givental conjecture==

The '''Arnold–Givental conjecture''', named after Vladimir Arnold and [[Alexander Givental]], gives a lower bound on the number of intersection points of two [[Lagrangian submanifold|Lagrangian submanifolds]] {{mvar|L}} and <math>L'</math> in terms of the Betti numbers of <math>L</math>, given that <math>L'</math> intersects {{mvar|L}} transversally and <math>L'</math> is Hamiltonian isotopic to {{mvar|L}}.

Let <math>(M, \omega)</math> be a compact <math>2n</math>-dimensional symplectic manifold, let <math>L \subset M</math> be a compact Lagrangian submanifold of <math>M</math>, and let <math>\tau : M \to M</math> be an anti-symplectic involution, that is, a diffeomorphism <math>\tau : M \to M</math> such that <math>\tau^* \omega = -\omega</math> and <math>\tau^2 = \text{id}_M</math>, whose fixed point set is <math>L</math>.

Let <math>H_t\in C^\infty(M)</math>, <math>t \in [0,1]</math> be a smooth family of [[Hamiltonian function]]s on <math>M</math>. This family generates a 1-parameter family of diffeomorphisms <math>\varphi_t: M \to M</math> by flowing along the [[Hamiltonian vector field]] associated to <math>H_t</math>. The Arnold–Givental conjecture states that if <math>\varphi_1(L)</math> intersects transversely with <math>L</math>, then

:<math>\# (\varphi_1(L) \cap L) \geq \sum_{i=0}^n \dim H_i(L; \mathbb Z / 2 \mathbb Z)</math>.<ref name="Frauenfelder">{{harv|Frauenfelder|2004}}</ref>

===Status===

The Arnold–Givental conjecture has been proved for several special cases.

* [[Alexander Givental]] proved it for <math>(M, L) = (\mathbb{CP}^n, \mathbb{RP}^n)</math>.<ref>{{harv|Givental|1989b}}</ref>
* [[Yong-Geun Oh]] proved it for real forms of compact Hermitian spaces with suitable assumptions on the [[Maslov index|Maslov indices]].<ref>{{harv|Oh|1995}}</ref>
* Lazzarini proved it for negative monotone case under suitable assumptions on the minimal Maslov number.
* [[Kenji Fukaya]], Yong-Geun Oh, Hiroshi Ohta, and [[Kaoru Ono]] proved it for <math>(M, \omega)</math> semi-positive.<ref>{{harv|Fukaya|Oh|Ohta|Ono|2009}}</ref>
* [[Urs Frauenfelder]] proved it in the case when <math>(M, \omega)</math> is a certain symplectic reduction, using [[Gauge theory (mathematics)|gauged]] [[Floer homology|Floer theory]].<ref name="Frauenfelder" />
